course_description:
This course develops engineering skills with the focus on planning, design, and construction of sustainable infrastructure with the key purpose to support and connect our communities. It is not simply the short-term provision of infrastructure that is of prime importance but planning and designing infrastructure which takes full account of its own impact and its operational needs and use. Sustainable infrastructure design is not just about new infrastructure, it is about rehabilitation, reuse, or optimisation of existing infrastructure. Infrastructure must be sustainable if it is to benefit coming generations and make a positive contribution to the future. Students will learn how to use their knowledge of these processes by designing sustainably and quantitatively assess alternative design options. Design-based problems and case studies are used to build on theory and challenge students to use their skills in applied settings. Current sustainability certification schemes are used in developing a framework for sustainable design and assessment, and students are taught how to apply these critically. This consistent with the principles of urban sustainability and global sustainable development goals..

Welcome to Sustainable Infrastructure Design, a course exploring the critical role of urban utilities, engineering, and treatment for future-proof communities. Through a blend of rigorous theoretical knowledge and practical applications, students will analyse real-world case studies, conduct in-depth research, and propose innovative solutions for modern water management. A central focus of this course is building a sophisticated awareness of localised infrastructure connectivity, training students to trace and audit the holistic interconnectedness of utility systems from individual dwellings up to institutional precinct scales. By stress-testing these networks, students will evaluate the structural, volumetric, and economic scalability effects of sudden density surges. Ultimately, this course equips students to transition from diagnostic analysis to engineering design, demonstrating how innovative, decentralised sustainable practices can be actively applied to support, secure, and future-proof the broader water system.

course_aims:
The aims of this course on Sustainable Infrastructure Design with a focus on water utilities, engineering, and treatment are as follows:

By the end of this course, students will be equipped with the knowledge and skills necessary to design and contribute to the development of sustainable water infrastructure systems.

learning_outcomes.description: To understand the fundamental principles and concepts of sustainable water infrastructure design.
To explore the different components and elements of water infrastructure systems, including utilities, engineering techniques, and treatment methods.
To analyse and evaluate the performance of existing water infrastructure systems and identify areas for improvement.
To apply sustainable design principles and practices in developing innovative solutions for water infrastructure projects.
To develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills in addressing the challenges and complexities of sustainable water infrastructure design.
To foster an understanding of the social, economic, and environmental impacts of water infrastructure and the importance of sustainability in decision-making.

assessment_details.title: In-Semester Examination
assessment_details.other_conditions: Time limited, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: The In-Semester Examination is an individually verified assessment designed to evaluate students' understanding of the fundamental principles, theories, and analytical methods underpinning sustainable infrastructure design. The examination focuses on the core concepts introduced during the course. Students will be required to demonstrate technical knowledge, interpret engineering scenarios, analyse infrastructure systems, and justify engineering decisions using evidence-based reasoning. The examination establishes the theoretical foundation for the remainder of the course by ensuring that each student has individually demonstrated competency before progressing to the major design project. Questions will assess students' understanding of engineering principles, their ability to critically analyse existing infrastructure, and their capacity to apply sustainable engineering concepts to realistic scenarios. This assessment task is to be completed in-person. The use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) tools will not be permitted. Any attempted use of AI or MT may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Individual Checkpoint
assessment_details.task_description: The Individual Checkpoint is a formative assessment milestone requiring students to submit the preliminary components of their final design project for review and feedback. Students will submit their engineering analysis, infrastructure audit, proposed design methodology, preliminary calculations, and initial sustainable engineering solution. This assessment verifies individual progress, confirms the technical feasibility of the proposed approach, and ensures that students are applying appropriate engineering principles before progressing to the final stage of the project. Students will be assessed on the quality of their engineering analysis, justification of assumptions, application of sustainable design principles, and their ability to critically evaluate alternative design solutions. Feedback will be provided to strengthen the technical quality of the project and guide further development. Students are expected to incorporate this feedback into their Individual Final Report , demonstrating refinement of their design through critical reflection, technical improvement, and evidence-based engineering judgement. Students may appropriately use AI and/or ML in completing this assessment task. Students must clearly reference any use of AI or ML in each instance. A failure to reference generative AI or ML use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Read full task description Hide full task description
assessment_details.assessment_security: Open assessment: In this assessment you can use resources such as your notes, course materials, and other tools, including AI, while completing the task. The focus is not on memorising information, but on understanding, applying judgement, and demonstrating your own thinking.

assessment_details.title: Individual Final Report
assessment_details.task_description: The Individual Final Report is the capstone assessment for the course and represents the culmination of the semester-long design project. Building on the knowledge demonstrated in the In-Semester Examination and the feedback received during the Individual Checkpoint, students will produce a comprehensive professional engineering report proposing an innovative and sustainable infrastructure solution. The report will demonstrate the complete engineering design process, including technical analysis, design development, sustainability assessment, evaluation of alternative solutions, and evidence-based recommendations. Students are expected to demonstrate advanced engineering judgement by integrating technical, environmental, economic, and social considerations into a coherent and professionally presented design solution. The report should reflect professional engineering practice through rigorous technical justification, critical evaluation of design decisions, effective communication, and incorporation of feedback received during the checkpoint milestone to demonstrate continuous improvement throughout the design process. Students may appropriately use AI and/or ML in completing this assessment task. Students must clearly reference any use of AI or ML in each instance.
